## Featurizing Medical history

We have the history of when which ICD codes were assigned to each patient, so we can featurize this time series to get the following sets of values per patient.

### Describe Basic Feature of Medical History

Now we can add features derived from each patients medical history. 
Here the "history" is every time they were assigned a unique ICD code on a specific date,
so a 2-column tibble with the columns `encounter_date` and `ICD_code`. 
From such a table we can compute the following features and what they may represent to our models

| Feature Name | Definition | Interpretation |
|--------------|:-----------|:---------------|
 `n_codes` | total codes assigned (unique date + code) ||
 `n_unique_codes` | unique codes assigned |  how many conditions does the patient have? health "prior"? |
 `history_length` | time between first and most recent visit | extensive medical history? many conditions? access to healthcare? |
 `n_visits` |  number of unique visits recorded | same as length, but maybe better |
 `most_common_code` |  which code was assigned the most frequently to the patient | their longest known condition? (appears on multiple visits) |
 `most_common_code.freq` | how frequently the most common code was assigned out of all codes assigned | how long they've known about theyre longest known condition (# of visits |
`code_frequency` | n_codes / history_length | |

: How we featurize each patient's medical history {tbl-colwidth="[10,40,50]"}


- can compute a cumulative distribution over time i.e. number total codes assigned & number unique codes assigned
- burstiness: did the patient have a single encounter where they gained lots of codes? i.e. big medical change?
